target: Ayez confiance en vous !
english: Have confidence in yourselves!
tip: French 'has' confidence rather than being confident: avoir confiance en = to trust. Ayez confiance en vous = have faith in yourselves.

target: Réfléchis bien avant de répondre.
english: Think carefully before answering.
tip: Only -er verbs drop the -s in the 'tu' command. '-ir' verbs keep it: 'réfléchis', not 'réfléchi'.

target: Il va pleuvoir cet après-midi.
english: It's going to rain this afternoon.
tip: The 'il' in il va pleuvoir is a placeholder, not a person – like the 'it' in 'it's raining'. Weather verbs like pleuvoir never take a real subject.

target: Asseyez-vous et attendez votre tour.
english: Sit down and wait for your turn.
tip: 'Asseyez-vous' – reflexive imperative: the pronoun goes after with a hyphen. Negative: 'ne vous asseyez pas'.

target: Dis-moi ce qui ne va pas.
english: Tell me what's wrong.
tip: 'What's wrong' is literally 'what isn't going': ce qui ne va pas. The verb aller (to go) doubles as 'to be OK' – ça va = it's going/fine.

target: Tu as reçu mon message ?
english: Did you receive my message?
tip: No question word needed – just a rising tone and a '?'. Tu as reçu mon message ? is a full yes/no question, same words as the statement.

target: Fais tes devoirs avant de jouer.
english: Do your homework before playing.
tip: 'Before' + an action needs 'de' plus the plain verb: avant de jouer = before playing. French uses the infinitive where English uses the -ing form.

target: Rangez vos affaires avant de partir.
english: Put away your things before leaving.
tip: 'Affaires' isn't 'affairs' – it means your things or belongings. Rangez vos affaires = put away your stuff.

target: Je paierai l'addition, c'est mon tour.
english: I'll pay the bill, it's my turn.
tip: 'L'addition' is the restaurant bill, not a maths sum. Je paierai l'addition = I'll pay the bill. You ask for it with 'L'addition, s'il vous plaît'.

target: Écoute-moi quand je te parle !
english: Listen to me when I'm talking to you!
tip: French has no separate '-ing' tense: je te parle means both 'I talk to you' and 'I'm talking to you'. Context tells you which.

target: Tu pourrais me rendre un service ?
english: Could you do me a favor?
tip: 'Pouvoir' in conditional: 'tu pourrais' (you could). Very common for polite requests.

target: Donne-moi la main pour traverser la rue.
english: Give me your hand to cross the street.
tip: French uses 'the' for body parts, not 'your': Donne-moi la main = give me your hand (literally 'the hand'). The owner is already obvious.

target: Monte dans la voiture, on est pressés.
english: Get in the car, we're in a hurry.
tip: In everyday French 'on' means 'we': on est pressés = we're in a hurry. It takes a singular verb (est) even though it means us.

target: Quand nous aurons économisé assez d'argent, nous voyagerons.
english: When we've saved enough money, we'll travel.
tip: After 'quand' French uses the future where English uses the present: quand nous aurons économisé = 'when we've saved'. Both clauses stay future.

target: Elles vont passer la soirée chez des amis.
english: They're going to spend the evening at friends' house.
tip: 'Chez' means 'at someone's place' in one word: chez des amis = at friends' house. No English equivalent – it always points to a person's home or shop.

target: Tu auras besoin de ton passeport pour ce voyage.
english: You'll need your passport for this trip.
tip: French doesn't 'need' – it 'has need of': avoir besoin de. Tu auras besoin de ton passeport = you'll need your passport. Always followed by de.

target: Si tu lui parlais, je suis sûr qu'il comprendrait.
english: If you talked to him, I'm sure he would understand.
tip: For an unreal 'if', 'si' takes the imperfect and the result takes the conditional: 'si tu lui parlais... il comprendrait' – never 'si' + conditional.

target: Je vais lui offrir un livre pour son anniversaire.
english: I'm going to give him a book for his birthday.
tip: 'Offrir' means to give as a gift, not to 'offer': lui offrir un livre = to give him a book. A present is always offrir, never donner.

target: On va commander une pizza, ça te va ?
english: We're going to order a pizza, is that okay with you?
tip: Nothing slots between 'aller' and the infinitive – no 'à', no 'de', despite English 'going TO order': 'on va commander une pizza'.

target: Je vais préparer le dîner pendant que tu te reposes.
english: I'm going to make dinner while you rest.
tip: 'Je vais préparer' – futur proche: aller (present) + infinitive. Natural in everyday speech.

target: Ils avaient essayé plusieurs restaurants avant de trouver le bon.
english: They had tried several restaurants before finding the right one.
tip: 'Avaient essayé' is the 'had done' past – one step further back than a past event. They had already tried several places before finding le bon (the right one).

target: Ne vous inquiétez pas, tout ira bien.
english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
tip: Negative reflexive imperative: Ne + pronoun + verb + pas. Ne vous inquiétez pas.

target: Elle aimerait vivre à Paris un jour.
english: She would like to live in Paris someday.
tip: The conditional softens a blunt wish: 'elle aimerait vivre' = she'd like to live, gentler than 'elle aime' or 'elle veut'.

target: Ça vaudrait le coup d'essayer.
english: It would be worth trying.
tip: Valoir le coup is literally 'to be worth the blow' – the everyday way to say something's worth it. Ça vaudrait le coup = it'd be worth it.

target: Nous allons partir dans cinq minutes.
english: We're going to leave in five minutes.
tip: For time still to come, dans means 'in', not 'within': dans cinq minutes = five minutes from now, not sometime in the next five.

target: L'avion décollera à quinze heures trente.
english: The plane will take off at three thirty.
tip: 'Décollera' – futur simple for scheduled events (flights, trains). Common in announcements.

target: Tu finiras par comprendre, ne t'inquiète pas.
english: You'll end up understanding, don't worry.
tip: "Finir par" + infinitive = to end up doing something. Finiras = futur simple of finir.

target: L'été prochain, il fera sûrement très chaud.
english: Next summer, it will surely be very hot.
tip: French weather runs on faire (to make): il fera très chaud is literally 'it will make very hot'. Same for cold and wind – il fera froid.

target: Elle va commencer un nouveau travail lundi.
english: She's going to start a new job on Monday.
tip: French drops the 'on' before weekdays: lundi alone means 'on Monday'. Add le – le lundi – and it flips to 'on Mondays', every week.

target: Quand j'aurai terminé, je passerai te voir.
english: When I'm done, I'll come by to see you.
tip: Where English says 'when I'm done', French looks ahead: quand j'aurai terminé is literally 'when I will have finished'. Future stacks on future.
